intro.data: Pair a thing with itself and you get a duplicator. Build the Diagonal that copies the name into a pair of IDENTICAL copies — so both projections return the original. One machine makes a true twin; the other makes a mismatched pair. Pick the real Diagonal.
intro.alchemy: Pair a thing with itself and you get a duplicator. Build the Diagonal that copies the salt into identical twins. One makes a true twin; the other a mismatch. Pick the real Diagonal.
intro.spellcraft: Pair a thing with itself and you get a duplicator. Build the Diagonal that copies the light into identical twins. One is a true twin; the other a mismatch. Pick the real Diagonal.
intro.abstract: Δ = ⟨id, id⟩ : A→A×A. Pick the one that makes an equal pair, so π₁∘Δ = π₂∘Δ = id.

goal.data: Duplicate the name into an identical pair.
goal.alchemy: Duplicate the salt into identical twins.
goal.spellcraft: Duplicate the light into identical twins.
goal.abstract: Build A×A as two equal copies of A.

afterSuccess.data: The Diagonal made two identical copies, so projecting either side gives back the original — π₁∘Δ = π₂∘Δ = id. The mismatched pair would fail that. The product gives you faithful duplication for free.
afterSuccess.alchemy: The Diagonal made identical twins; either projection gives back the salt. The mismatch would fail. The product gives duplication for free.
afterSuccess.spellcraft: The Diagonal made identical twins; either projection gives back the light. The mismatch would fail. The product gives duplication for free.
afterSuccess.abstract: Δ = ⟨id, id⟩, so π₁∘Δ = π₂∘Δ = id. The mismatched pair is not the diagonal.

reveal.summary: The diagonal Δ : A → A×A pairs an object with itself; both projections recover the original: π₁∘Δ = π₂∘Δ = id_A.
reveal.moreFormal: The diagonal is the pairing of identity with itself — duplication, available in any category with products.
reveal.programmerAnalogy: const dup = (x) => [x, x]; both [0] and [1] return x.
